sheets.prompt:
Image 1 is a sticker of a cheerful lilac-and-cream Pachycephalosaurus standing on its two back legs, turned a little to the left, with a big smooth round cream dome on top of its head ringed with little soft rounded bumps. Draw this exact Pachycephalosaurus as a cut-out paper puppet: its separate body parts laid out on one sheet, the same drawing style, colours, texture, line and proportions as in image 1, every part at the size it has in image 1.

Draw each part on its own, spread out over the sheet with wide empty gaps between them, no part touching or overlapping another:
1. the body with its neck: the lilac body with its cream tummy and cream throat and its darker purple spots, turned as in image 1, without head, without arms, without legs and without tail: no arms, hands, legs or feet drawn on it, the tummy one smooth round shape. At the top, the cream throat and the lilac spotted back of the neck go up as in image 1, as wide as the neck is just under the head, and end in a soft, smooth edge with NO outline (it is hidden under the head). At the back, the spotted back runs on smoothly into the very root of the tail and ends there in a soft edge cut straight down, with NO outline across it (the tail tucks under it): no round bump, no stump, no line where the tail would join. The drawing's dark outline runs only along the front of the neck and chest, round the tummy and along the back.
2. the head alone with its dome, without neck: the head with its rounded lilac snout, its two little nostrils, the rosy cheek, the purple spots, the big smooth round cream dome on top and the ring of little soft rounded cream bumps round it, turned as in image 1, the dome and every bump drawn whole. A completely blank face: no eyes, no eyebrows, no mouth and no mouth line, the snout and the cream jaw one smooth closed shape; keep the nostrils, the rosy cheek and the little bump of the head's outline where the far eye sits by the snout. Keep its dark outline round the dome and bumps, round the snout and along the jaw under the snout to the chin, as in image 1. From the chin round to the back of the neck its bottom edge is soft, with NO outline: the cream throat and the lilac back of the neck simply stop there, a little below the rosy cheek.
3. the far little arm: the little arm on the left of image 1, behind the chest, drawn whole from the top of its shoulder (normally hidden behind the chest) down to its little hand with soft, round, blunt mauve fingertips, hanging as in image 1; its top a full, smooth, rounded end with no outline across it.
4. the near little arm: the little arm on the right of image 1, held in front of the chest, drawn whole from the top of its shoulder (normally hidden in the chest) down to its little hand with soft, round, blunt mauve fingertips, hanging as in image 1; its top a full, smooth, rounded end with no outline across it.
5. the far leg: the leg on the left of image 1, drawn whole from the top of its thigh (normally hidden behind the round tummy) down to its foot with soft, round, blunt mauve toes, as in image 1; its top a full, smooth, rounded end with no outline across it.
6. the near leg: the big leg on the right of image 1, drawn whole from the top of its big round thigh down to its foot with soft, round, blunt mauve toes, as in image 1, the round thigh with its whole outline as in image 1.
7. the tail: the long tapering spotted tail with its cream underside, as in image 1, drawn whole from its thick root (normally hidden inside the body) to its rounded tip; its root a soft, smooth edge cut straight across with NO outline.

Every part is drawn whole, including what is normally hidden behind another part, and each joint end (where it tucks under the body or the head) is a full, smooth, rounded edge. Nothing sharp: no teeth, no pointed claws, no spikes. No text, no labels, no numbers, no outline around the parts beyond the drawing's own line, no shadows. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a cheerful lilac-and-cream Pachycephalosaurus with a big round dome on its head; image 2 shows the same Pachycephalosaurus cut into puppet parts, with a blank face. Draw the Pachycephalosaurus's face pieces as separate stickers on one sheet: the same drawing style, colours and line as in image 1, every piece at the size it has on the Pachycephalosaurus in image 1, so it fits the blank face in image 2. Its head is turned to the left: its far eye (on the left of image 1, just above the snout, on the head's outline) is smaller and narrower than its near eye (on the right of image 1). In image 1 both eyes look up and to the left: each dark-brown iris with its white sparkle sits towards the upper left of its eye, the white on its right, outlined in dark brown.

Draw each piece on its own, upright, in four tidy rows with wide empty gaps between them, nothing touching:
Row 1, the far eye (the smaller narrow eye, on the LEFT of image 1), six times:
1. as it is in image 1: a small tall oval eye, its big dark-brown iris with a white sparkle towards the upper left, a little white on its right, outlined in dark brown.
2. wide open and surprised: bigger and rounder, a warm-brown iris with a dark pupil and a white sparkle, looking the same way.
3. closed in a happy smile: an upward-curving arc, like an upside-down U, with two little lashes.
4. sad: open and round, a soft warm-brown iris with a white sparkle and a thin shine of a welling tear along its bottom rim, looking down and to the left; no lid slanting across it.
5. crying: squeezed shut, a thick lid line as wide as the open eye, curving down at both ends like a little frown, and one small light-blue teardrop just below its outer (left) end.
6. gently closed in sleep: a soft downward-curving line as wide as the open eye, with a few short lashes.
Row 2, the near eye (the bigger eye, on the RIGHT of image 1), the same six in the same order; open, it looks the same way as row 1, up and to the left, the iris towards the upper left of the eye; crying, its teardrop below its outer (right) end.
Row 3: 13. the far eyebrow (over the left eye of image 1) as it is in image 1, a short thin dark-brown arch. 14. the same far eyebrow worried: tilted up at its inner (right) end. 15. the near eyebrow (over the right eye of image 1) as it is in image 1, a thin dark-brown arch. 16. the same near eyebrow worried: tilted up at its inner (left) end.
Row 4, mouths, none with any teeth: 17. the mouth as it is in image 1: a long, thin, closed cheeky grin, gently curved, curling up into a little smile at its right end. 18. the mouth wide open in a big happy laugh, rounded, the inside pink with a little pink tongue, no teeth. 19. the mouth open in a small round 'o', the inside pink. 20. the mouth in a small sad frown, a closed line curving down. 21. the mouth wide open in a big round yawn, the inside pink with a little tongue, no teeth. 22. the mouth sobbing: a small open downturned frown with a little pink inside.

No text, no labels, no numbers, no shadows, no face or head around the pieces. Fully transparent background.
